current_root_conclusion: A shared slow execution-delivery state leaves the consumer without enough worst-state throughput margin. Real GIL/Qt waits coexist, but video/model isolation is not sufficient even in a severe process-first cold window. The physical cause remains unidentified.

matrix.question: Is the old PMC CPU share quantitatively usable?
matrix.evidence: 83.5967ms remains unresolved after lifecycle, clipping, duplicate and clock checks; old 31.25ms gate remains failed.
matrix.next: Do not compute CPU/GIL/cache/frequency contribution shares from the old four windows.

matrix.question: Where does field latency accumulate?
matrix.evidence: 1000Hz receipt remained accurate while pending age and contact-to-paint reached seconds; final drain does not restore real-time compliance.
matrix.next: Keep FIFO age and scheduled contact-to-paint as field endpoints.

matrix.question: Is a real GIL/Qt synchronization path present?
matrix.evidence: Consumer take_gil chains and Qt QLabel/latch overlap are retained; waiter stacks do not identify the holder or quantitative share.
matrix.next: Do not relabel all waiting or wall-minus-CPU as GIL.

matrix.question: Does video+MediaPipe process isolation give stable fast-state benefit?
matrix.evidence: Four timed pairs changed latency -3.6%, +0.9%, +5.5%, -5.3%; geometric change -0.69%, with process queue lower bounds slightly higher in all pairs.
matrix.next: Do not optimize or merge this boundary based on fast windows.

matrix.question: Is video+MediaPipe process isolation sufficient in a severe cold-first window?
matrix.evidence: The process-first cold window still reached queue lower/upper 1614/1694 and scheduled contact-to-paint 1491ms with input lateness 93ms.
matrix.next: Return to consumer worst-state service capacity; do not add more visual isolation windows.

matrix.question: Do model and consumer share a slow execution state?
matrix.evidence: Severe A/A model medians were 40.5-40.8ms with queue lower 3981-4239; fast A/A model medians 23.1-23.9ms with queue lower 91, while work counts differed only 3-4%. PMC also retained Core/OS about1.00 slow versus1.66-1.68 fast.
matrix.next: Name only execution-delivery state; frequency, cache, power, thermal and exact native function remain unknown.

matrix.question: Do process restart or five-minute quiet gaps control the state?
matrix.evidence: Six fixed-work windows stayed slow across 5s and qualified 300s low-load gaps; other GUI sequences recovered after two windows.
matrix.next: Do not add ordinary spacing windows.

hypothesis_ranking.hypothesis: Shared native/CPU execution-delivery state affects consumer and MediaPipe work
GIL acquisition and Qt/system synchronization add contention within that state
Moving video/model alone controls severe backlog
hypothesis_ranking.status: rejected as sufficient in a severe process-first cold window

hypothesis_ranking.hypothesis: USB/grating power state is the primary cause
hypothesis_ranking.status: weak field correlation only; host saved-input severe state exists without live USB

next_minimal_validation.scope: Read-only worst-state consumer capacity derivation from retained severe windows; no new workload.
inputs: cold process-first queue timeline and receipts
retained batch boundaries, consumer CPU/cycles and contact publications
outputs: arrival rate, effective drain rate and queue growth by phase
required per-frame/batch service margin for 1000Hz and <=250-frame FIFO
code-stage candidates whose measured cost can close that margin

decisions.software_capacity_root: consumer service rate falls below 1000Hz in severe windows even after video/model isolation
decisions.next_candidate: only a surgical stage with enough measured margin may enter offline A/B
decisions.insufficient: no stage-level evidence large enough to close the measured deficit

constraints: No new reboot,human,USB,Run or ordinary fast-state window
No CPU/GIL/frequency percentage from failed PMC accounting
No formal optimization until an offline candidate meets the required margin and semantics
